s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with fever and vomiting
salient_findings: Rigid abdomen with diffuse severe tenderness
Air–fluid levels in the small bowel on abdominal radiograph
Hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region on ultrasonography
key_facts: 18-hour history of symptoms
Fever of 39 °C
Vomiting
Constipation
Unremarkable past medical history
Normal hemoglobin, white-cell and platelet counts
Normal prothrombin time, INR, glucose, creatinine, urea, sodium, and potassium
Elevated C-reactive protein at 134.5 mg/L
Rigid abdomen with diffuse severe tenderness on examination
Soft stool without blood on digital rectal examination
Normal chest examination
Air–fluid levels in the small bowel on erect abdominal radiograph
Dilated large-bowel loops on abdominal radiograph
5-cm hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region on ultrasonography
Hyperdense midline mass above the bladder on non-contrast abdominal CT

shortlist.label: Intussusception
shortlist.why_kept: 5-cm hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region surrounded by intestinal loops on ultrasonography, consistent with intussusception

shortlist.label: Acute appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Rigid abdomen with diffuse severe tenderness, fever, and elevated C-reactive protein

shortlist.label: Meckel's diverticulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Abdominal pain, fever, and vomiting, with a possible Meckel's diverticulum causing inflammation

shortlist.label: Small bowel obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Air–fluid levels in the small bowel on erect abdominal radiograph, indicating possible obstruction

shortlist.label: Midgut volvulus
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperdense midline mass above the bladder on non-contrast abdominal CT, which could be related to midgut volvulus

raw.rationale: The presence of a 5-cm hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region surrounded by intestinal loops on ultrasonography, along with air–fluid levels in the small bowel and dilated large-bowel loops on abdominal radiograph, is highly suggestive of intussusception, which is a condition where a part of the intestine telescopes into another part.

rejected.label: Acute appendicitis
rejected.why: While acute appendicitis can cause abdominal pain and fever, the presence of a hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region and air–fluid levels in the small bowel is more indicative of intussusception.

rejected.label: Meckel's diverticulitis
rejected.why: Meckel's diverticulitis typically presents with pain and inflammation in the right lower quadrant, which is not consistent with the diffuse severe tenderness and hypogastric mass seen in this case.

rejected.label: Small bowel obstruction
rejected.why: While small bowel obstruction can cause abdominal pain, vomiting, and constipation, the presence of a hyperechoic mass and air–fluid levels is more specific for intussusception.

rejected.label: Midgut volvulus
rejected.why: Midgut volvulus typically presents with bilious vomiting and abdominal tenderness, but the presence of a hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region is more indicative of intussusception.
